### `api.dcc.maya.align_clavicle_to_upperarm_height(...)`

- Target: `maya_tools.Rigging.mocap.setup_hik.align_clavicle_to_upperarm_height`
- Signature: `align_clavicle_to_upperarm_height(`
- API names: `align_clavicle_to_upperarm_height`
- Args:
  - `clavicle_joint`, required
  - `upperarm_joint`, required
  - `sample_range`, default `30.0`
  - `step`, default `0.1`
- Related functions:
  - same_module: [`api.dcc.maya.align_clavicle_Y_by_rotateY(...)`](#apidccmayaalign_clavicle_y_by_rotatey) -> `maya_tools.Rigging.mocap.setup_hik.align_clavicle_Y_by_rotateY` - Shares module and name terms; may be useful in the same workflow.; source [setup_hik.py:225](C:/depot/tools/maya_tools/Rigging/mocap/setup_hik.py:225)
- Description: Level clavicle local X in front view with a pure world-Z rotation. The studio clavicle frame uses local Y for its authored forward/back roll and local Z close to world vertical. Rotating whichever local axis merely happens to be closest to world depth can therefore swing the clavicle forward. A world-Z rotation changes only its front-view elevation while preserving the reference-rig depth component and roll convention.
- Source: [setup_hik.py:269](C:/depot/tools/maya_tools/Rigging/mocap/setup_hik.py:269)

Brow landmarks are independent children of the head, so a generic local surface transfer can accidentally fold ``brow_end`` back toward the eye. - Description: Move each arm root from the torso seed to the humeral-head section. A globally scaled template commonly leaves the upper-arm pivot inside the chest. In a T/A pose, the torso-to-arm transition is measurable: the very tall torso section collapses into a compact, nearly round deltoid/humeral section. Search only the proximal third of the upper arm and take the first local section matching that morphology. This is a 3D volume test, not a front-view silhouette estimate.

- Description: Fit neck, skull, jaw, teeth, and tongue without surface extrapolation. These pivots sit inside the skull or oral cavity, where nearest-surface patches are frequently close to planar. A local affine solve can then become ill-conditioned and throw the joint toward the face. Blend the normalized authored pivots from the closest topology-compatible rigs instead; this keeps the centerline stable while retaining age/proportion differences from the reference corpus.
